Given that the ray above passes through the point with Cartesian coordinates $(-3,3\sqrt{3}),$ find the polar equation of the ray. Assume that the polar angle is in the range $[0,2\pi ).$

$\theta =$ 
 {{field-1}}.
worked_solution:
First, we find the reference angle associated with the point:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\theta }_{R} & =\operatorname{arctan}⁡|\frac{y}{x}| \\  & =\operatorname{arctan}⁡|\frac{3\sqrt{3}}{(-3)}| \\  & =\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\sqrt{3}) \\  & =\frac{\pi }{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, notice that the ray lies in the second quadrant. So, we find the angle in the second quadrant that has a reference angle ${\theta }_{R}=\frac{\pi }{3}$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\theta  & =\pi -{\theta }_{R} \\  & =\pi -\frac{\pi }{3} \\  & =\frac{2\pi }{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the polar equation of the ray is 

$$
\theta =\frac{2\pi }{3}.
$$
